bug.title: LLMSignalAuthor hands the anti-convergence gate raw proposal.md text instead of prior code, so an exact repeat of a prior signal is admitted as novel
bug.symptoms: LLMSignalAuthor checks each answer with anti_convergence.admit(parsed.code, held=held), where held carries the history's prior proposals as raw proposal.md text: a Mechanism line, prose and a ```python fence. The gate compares source structure with its numbers erased. Markdown is not Python source, so nothing matches. Probe: with a prior proposal "Mechanism: momentum" wrapping the source `def signal(ctx, seed): return ctx.closes().pct_change()`, an answer repeating that exact source is admitted on the first call. - admit(src, held=[("n1", markdown)]) gives reason "novel". - admit(src, held=[("n1", src)]) gives reason "parameter_tweak". The anti-convergence safeguard (feature 210; architecture section 14.1: "a converged tree is not caught by anything") is therefore silently disabled for every live authoring.
bug.reproduction_steps: Build an LLMSignalAuthor with the real "signal-agent-anti-convergence" gate, and a history store whose single prior proposal wraps source S in a ```python fence. Answer the first call with the same fenced S. The author returns it without a retry.
bug.expected: - held is built from each prior proposal's code: (node_id, parse_authored(prior.proposal).code) for every prior whose proposal parses. - A prior whose proposal does not parse (AuthoredOutputError) contributes (node_id, prior.code_hash) when its code_hash is non-blank, a digest form the gate accepts, and is skipped otherwise. - An answer whose code repeats a prior's structure, with only its numbers changed or with none changed, is refused by the gate. The refusal goes through the existing retry path, naming the gate's reason code (parameter_tweak), and AuthoringRefusedError follows after max_retries. - A genuinely different signal is still admitted on the first call. - Tests cover an exact repeat, a numbers-only tweak, a novel signal, and an unparsable prior proposal, all with the real gate.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/signal-agent/src/signal_agent/_llm_author.py builds held from PriorProposal.proposal, the raw markdown, rather than from the code extracted from it. additions_spec_llm_authoring.xml feature 7 said "held=the history's prior proposals" without saying which part.
bug.constraints: Every other behaviour of LLMSignalAuthor and its existing tests is kept No network access and no real credential in any test No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/

bug.title: LLMReviser's identical-to-incumbent check compares raw strings, so an unchanged module differing only in a trailing newline is accepted as a revision
bug.symptoms: dreaming.llm_reviser refuses an answer identical to the incumbent with `if code == incumbent_source:` (line 427). The extracted fenced block never carries the incumbent's trailing newline. So with incumbent "def select(view):\n return []\n" and the answer ```python + that same module + ```, the revision is accepted and revise_policy yields a candidate identical to the incumbent. Whitespace-only differences pass the same way: CRLF line endings, trailing spaces, and leading or trailing blank lines.
bug.reproduction_steps: LLMReviser over a fake provider answering the incumbent's own source in a python fence. Call revise_policy(incumbent, 1, reviser=reviser). One candidate is returned, where ReviserOutputError was expected.
bug.expected: - Before comparing, both texts are normalised: CRLF to LF, trailing whitespace stripped from every line, and leading and trailing blank lines dropped. - An answer equal to the incumbent after normalisation raises ReviserOutputError (code word reviser_output) naming revision_index. - A change of any token, including inside a string or a comment, is still accepted as a revision. - Tests cover a trailing-newline-only difference, CRLF, trailing spaces, extra blank lines (all refused), and a one-character change (accepted).
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/dreaming/src/dreaming/llm_reviser.py compares the extracted code with the incumbent by exact string equality.
bug.constraints: Every other behaviour of LLMReviser and its existing tests is kept No network access and no real credential in any test No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
